title: The Battery Data Commons registry
source: Joule
abstract: Public battery datasets are growing rapidly, but fragmented hosting and inconsistent descriptions make them difficult to find, compare, and reuse. Battery Data Commons presently indexes 349 datasets in a living, searchable metadata registry, using human- and machine-readable descriptions linked to the original sources. This exposes experimental context without relocating raw data to give datasets wider visibility and a second life to legacy ones. Together, these capabilities provide infrastructure for reproducible battery science, engineering, and AI-enabled innovation.

title: Coherent manipulation of Zr(III) aryloxide qudits
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Paramagnetic molecules can serve as electron spin qubits for quantum information processing, provided that they preserve their spin coherence for a sufficient time to allow for computation and error correction. Here we report the rare isolation of stable Zr(III) aryloxide complexes, where Zr is an earth-abundant metal ion with a coherently manipulable electron spin. Density functional theory calculations reveal the trigonal planar d1 geometry stabilizes a 4dz2–5s hybrid singly occupied molecular orbital with little ligand contribution and significant s character (25–27%), yielding large isotropic hyperfine coupling constants of 803–809 MHz. We observed long spin–lattice relaxation times (T1) up to 87 ms and dephasing times (Tm, TmCPMG) up to 123 μs using isotope-selective pulsed electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy. Nutation experiments further showed coherent manipulation of several electronic and electronuclear transitions. This study introduces Zr(III) aryloxides as competitive molecular qudits and expands the scope of metal ions to more earth-abundant metals.

title: Unveiling the role of crystallinity of RuO2 catalysts for regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: The intrinsic role of crystallinity in regulating the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) on RuO2 remains elusive due to the synthetic challenge of decoupling structural order from compositional variations. Here, we develop an oxygen-partial-pressure-controlled pyrolysis strategy to achieve graded crystallinity in pure RuO2 nanocatalysts, establishing a pristine model to elucidate this structure-function relationship. We reveal that amorphous RuO2 features disordered dangling oxygen that readily undergoes protonation, triggering a rapid but degradative lattice oxygen-mediated mechanism (LOM) with an ultralow overpotential of 154 mV at 10 mA cm−2. Conversely, increasing crystallinity stabilizes the RuO6 framework, suppressing protonation and shifting the pathway toward the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM). Crucially, highly crystalline RuO2 demands excessive cell voltages (1.72 V at 1.0 A cm−2) in proton exchange membrane electrolyzers, paradoxically accelerating oxidative etching. This work uncovers a crystallinity-driven LOM-to-AEM transition, identifying intermediate crystallinity as a practical strategy for balancing activity and stability.

title: Two pathways driving Phanerozoic temperature change: low-latitude radiative forcing and outgassing-weathering-vegetation carbon feedbacks
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Two potentially interacting pathways may have shaped Phanerozoic temperature change: radiative effects linked to low-latitude land area and carbon-cycle feedbacks involving volcanic outgassing, silicate weathering, and terrestrial organic-carbon burial. Together, these processes provide a framework for understanding long-term climate evolution over the past 540 million years.

title: A Full-Duplex Metasurface for Simultaneous and Independent Control of Radiation and Reflection
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Metasurfaces have transformed electromagnetic interfaces from fixed, material-defined boundaries into engineered platforms for tailoring wave propagation, spanning both passive designs and actively programmable implementations. For future information systems, a central challenge is to make the same physical aperture operate simultaneously as a radiating antenna and a reconfigurable reflector. Radiation–reflection-integrated (R2I) metasurfaces combine these functions, but their responses remain coupled: configuring the surface for radiation constrains its behavior in reflection. They therefore cannot generally provide independent operation at the same time, frequency, and polarization. Here, we show an intelligent full-duplex R2I metasurface that overcomes this constraint. The surface integrates controllable meta-atoms with a substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW). Because the SIW-guided and free-space excitations occupy largely separated regions of the spatial spectrum, the radiated and reflected fields can be manipulated simultaneously and independently on the same aperture. We experimentally demonstrate this capability in integrated sensing and communication and in integrated detection and stealth, both realized using a single artificial-intelligence-assisted metasurface under identical operating conditions. These results establish a route towards full-duplex, single-aperture information systems.

title: Metastable synchronization and inertial-beating sensing in nonlinear oscillators
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Synchronization is widely used to enhance the sensitivity and noise resilience of mechanical sensors, while nonlinear operation is often assumed to substantially broaden the usable synchronization bandwidth. Here, we show that this apparent bandwidth enhancement is fundamentally metastable. In nonlinear self-oscillating systems, large portions of the nominal synchronization region are dynamically inaccessible under direct signal injection, despite being theoretically stable. We demonstrate that this breakdown originates from phase inertia, which endows phase evolution with an effective second-order response and creates inertial barriers to phase capture. As a result, nonlinear synchronization splits into a narrow dynamically accessible locking region and a much larger metastable regime in which stable phase locking exists in principle but cannot be reached in practice. Rather than suppressing this inertial unlocking behavior, we exploit it as a sensing mechanism. Near the inaccessible locking boundary, phase inertia sustains slow beating dynamics that continuously encode frequency detuning while intrinsically averaging fast phase fluctuations. The resulting inertial-beating transduction produces a continuous, history-independent sensing response and enables faster synchronization dynamics beyond the conventional locking regime. More broadly, our results reveal that synchronization bandwidth is fundamentally governed by dynamical accessibility rather than static stability, establishing phase inertia as a general organizing principle for nonlinear synchronization dynamics across driven oscillatory systems.

title: The Evolution of Brain-Computer Interfaces Towards Collaborative Intelligence
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are evolving from unidirectional control toward deeper integration of biological and machine intelligence. This transition is constrained by two complementary bottlenecks: Intent Mismatch, or Brain-to-Machine Underreach, in which user intentions cannot be sufficiently decoded, represented, or executed by the machine; and State Mismatch, or Machine-to-Brain Overload, in which system demands exceed the user’s current cognitive, affective, or neural resources. This review uses these two mismatches as an organizing framework for examining the evolution of BCIs toward brain-machine collaborative intelligence, while distinguishing non-invasive and invasive modalities according to their signal characteristics and translational constraints. We review neural decoding, generative artificial intelligence, and shared control as approaches for reducing Intent Mismatch, and passive BCIs, adaptive interaction, neurofeedback, and neuromodulation as approaches for reducing State Mismatch. By integrating these solution paths, this review outlines a pathway toward adaptive, bidirectional, and human-centered BCI systems.

title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Aqueous redox flow batteries are promising for large-scale grid energy storage, but their widespread implementation is hindered by the lack of anolyte materials that combine high capacity, environmental compatibility, recyclability, low cost and long-term stability. While organic anolyte molecules offer a potential sustainable solution, integrating these competing attributes within a single molecular platform remains challenging. Here we report a recyclable oligo(disulfide)-based anolyte in which robust sulfur–sulfur bonds serve as redox-active sites. The anolyte is synthesized by ring-opening polymerization of potassium-form endogenous thioctic acid, providing a scalable route to high-concentration redox-active species. Paired with a sulfonated cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst, this oligo(disulfide) anolyte delivers a capacity density of 128 Ah l−1 with a 95.5% material utilization rate at 50 mA cm−2. Using a carbon-coated sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membrane with a sulfur–sulfur bond concentration of 0.25 M, the battery retains 98.1% of its capacity over 2,200 cycles while maintaining an energy efficiency of approximately 70% at 100 mA cm−2. We further validate the scalability and closed-loop recyclability of this chemistry in a 63 Wh stack. Our findings establish oligo(disulfide)s as a robust, circular redox platform, providing a pathway towards more resource-efficient and sustainable grid-scale energy storage.

title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: As an energy-efficient and scalable alternative to conventional chemical absorption, membrane-based carbon capture requires materials that simultaneously combine molecular-level thinness, precise sub-nanometre porosity and exceptional mechanical robustness—a longstanding trilemma in separation science. Here we report graphene–amorphous carbon bilayer membranes that overcome these trade-offs by way of a graphene-guided polymer conversion approach. Leveraging a super-spreading effect, we coat graphene with a uniform, ultra-smooth, polymer-derived carbon layer as thin as 2 nm, achieving a high Young’s modulus of approximately 26.8 GPa. Controlled pyrolysis of the polymer precursor generates a carbon network featuring narrowly distributed, high-precision ultramicropores. The resulting graphene–amorphous carbon membranes exhibit sharp molecular sieving (selectivity of >60 for CO2/N2, >70 for H2/CO2 and >70 for CO2/CH4) alongside an exceptional CO2 permeance of up to 5,000 gas permeation units that surpasses existing benchmarks. This combination of structural integrity and separation performance enables efficient carbon capture across varied flue gas, syngas and natural gas streams, establishing graphene–amorphous carbon membranes as a versatile, energy-efficient platform for sustainable molecular separations.

title: Harnessing protein conformational dynamics for next-generation supramolecular materials
source: Matter
abstract: Protein conformational dynamics govern how proteins assemble across distinct pathways. This review unifies native crystallization, amyloid fibrillization, and reduction-induced phase transitions, revealing how dynamic assembly routes can be harnessed to design adaptive, hierarchical protein materials with programmable functions.

title: Reversing Electrochemical Spongification by Asymmetric Breathing for 380‐hour Hydroxylamine Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic nitrate‐to‐hydroxylamine (NH
                    2
                    OH) conversion offers a sustainable route for reactive nitrogen upcycling. Metallic bismuth (Bi) is intrinsically active for this reaction, yet undergoes severe structural degradation under continuous electrolysis—a failure mode we identify as electrochemical spongification, wherein the compact Bi framework cathodically relaxes into an electrically disconnected porous network. Herein, we report an “asymmetric electrochemical breathing” strategy that effectively decouples long‐term catalytic durability from structural failure. Using pulsed potentials between −1.36 and +1.24 V versus the reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE), BiOCl nanosheets serve as a dynamic template, delivering a high Faradaic efficiency of 71.7% and a yield rate of 4.29 mmol h
                    −1
                    cm
                    −2
                    , among the highest reported for NH
                    2
                    OH electrosynthesis. Experimental and theoretical insights reveal that BiOCl rapidly reduces in situ to dense metallic Bi to drive efficient nitrate reduction. Crucially, a brief anodic pulse reconstructs the framework before irreversible degradation occurs, enabling continuous structural rejuvenation for over 380 h. This dynamic reconstruction strategy successfully suppresses the Faradaic efficiency decay rate by two orders of magnitude, establishing a robust paradigm for stabilizing highly active yet metastable electrocatalysts.

title: Electrosynthesis of p‐Hydroxybenzoic Acid From Phenol and CO2
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    P
                    ‐hydroxybenzoic acid (
                    p
                    ‐HBA), with wide applications in food preservatives, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and liquid crystalline polyether, is currently synthesized via the Kolbe–Schmitt reaction using anhydrous phenolate (PhO
                    −
                    ) and carbon dioxide (CO
                    2
                    ). However, this reaction typically suffers from poor selectivity, and requires high temperature/pressure, strongly base, and metal/organic cations for selectivity control. Herein, we report a new method for the electrosynthesis of
                    p
                    ‐HBA from phenol (PhOH) and CO
                    2
                    by iodine mediation, achieving 61% yield and 90% selectivity without strong bases and metal cations under ambient temperature and pressure conditions. Mechanism studies indicated that PhOH was first selectively iodinated by iodine cations (I
                    +
                    ) generated at the anode to form
                    p
                    ‐iodophenol (HOPh‐I). Subsequently, HOPh‐I and CO
                    2
                    were respectively activated on Ag catalyst with abundant grain boundaries (GB‐Ag) through single‐electron reduction, and then underwent radical coupling processes to produce
                    p

Notably, this electrochemical method also successfully converted various oxygen‐containing and nitrogen‐containing aromatic compounds, including the typical structural units of lignin and its derivatives, into valuable carboxylic acids. This innovative electrochemical approach overcomes the inherent limitations of the traditional Kolbe–Schmitt reaction, offering a promising strategy for the sustainable utilization of CO
                    2
                    and biomass resources.

source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT

Based on these findings, a novel design pathway for deep‐UV materials might be proposed, linking π‐conjugation degree and packing density with SHG and birefringence.

title: Ni3(HITP)2@PTFE Molecular Fence Enables Selective C2 Coupling in Methane Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Contact‐Electro‐Catalysis (CEC) enables methane activation under ambient conditions; however, the poorly understood interfacial active sites and uncontrolled evolution of reactive radical intermediates cause methane conversion to remain dominated by C
                    1
                    oxygenation rather than selective C─C coupling. Herein, we assemble the established Ni
                    3
                    (HITP)
                    2
                    framework (HITP = 2,3,6,7,10,11‐hexaiminotriphenylene) on PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene) to construct a molecular fence interface integrating Ni–N
                    4

                    2
                    coupling. During CEC, contact electrification at the PTFE–water interface supports radical generation for methane conversion, while the coupled Ni–N
                    4

title: On‐Surface Non‐Equilibrium Phase Evolution Toward 2D Supramolecular Glass
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Controlling crystalline‐to‐glassy transitions represents a vibrant frontier in supramolecular chemistry and condensed matter physics, providing fundamental insights into non‐equilibrium dynamics and enabling functional tunability for elasticity electronics and phase‐change devices. Conventional two‐dimensional (2D) supramolecular assembly follows an enthalpy‐dominated thermodynamic paradigm, restricting the exploration of non‐equilibrium supramolecular glasses (SMGs). Herein, we report the controlled construction of a non‐equilibrium SMG on Ag(111) using in situ‐generated triradical triphenyl‐triazine molecules. The electrophilic triazine core enriches charge density at radical sites and strengthens molecule–substrate interfacial coupling, imposing pronounced kinetic constraints at the surface. Upon thermal activation, the system follows a non‐monotonic, four‐phase evolution that involves a thermodynamically uphill transformation. Rather than directly relaxing to the global thermodynamic minimum, it is kinetically arrested into a metastable glassy state with short‐range order and long‐range disorder. This work revises the conventional enthalpy‐dominated view of supramolecular assembly and establishes a backbone‐modulated radical kinetic strategy for rational fabrication of disorder‐tunable 2D supramolecular materials.

title: Interfacial Charge Modulation of Covalent Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrochemical H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    synthesis through the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction offers a sustainable alternative to the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Crystalline porous frameworks are attractive for this route because of their structural precision, yet poor electrolyte wetting and limited electrochemical accessibility often restrict their practical performance. Here, we report an interfacial charge‐modulation strategy that transforms covalent metal–organic frameworks into highly wetted and electrochemically accessible catalytic interfaces. By incorporating cationic ethidium bromide units into a trinuclear copper‐pyrazolate framework, we construct EB‐Cu
                    3
                    ‐COF featuring enlarged interlayer spacing, enhanced interfacial charge transfer, and optimized *OOH intermediate adsorption. Consequently, EB‐Cu
                    3

                    2

                    cat
                    −1
                    ·h
                    −1
                    , ranking among the best‐performing non‐pyrolyzed porous organic electrocatalysts reported to date. This work establishes interfacial charge‐modulation as a design principle for translating crystalline structural precision into electrochemically active interfaces.

title: Aluminum Scandium Nitride (AlScN) for Advanced Devices: Physical Mechanisms and Emerging Applications
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  AlScN is an emerging semiconductor material that exhibits pronounced ferroelectric switching and enhanced piezoelectric responses through the incorporation of scandium (Sc) into aluminum nitride (AlN). These properties make AlScN a promising candidate for next‐generation ferroelectric in‐memory computing architecture and radio‐frequency circuits. However, challenges arise when preparing high‐quality epitaxial films with high Sc content, including insufficient ferroelectric endurance, interface instability, and leakage current, which collectively compromise device performance and reliability. This review provides a systematic overview of the ferroelectric and piezoelectric properties of AlScN with underlying physical mechanisms, highlights the challenges in material growth and device integration, and summarizes recent advances of emerging applications in piezoelectric devices, optoelectronic devices, ferroelectric memories, and high‐electron‐mobility transistors (HEMTs). Finally, perspectives are presented on future research directions, focusing on overcoming key barriers to device implementation. With ongoing advances in material optimization and system‐level integration, AlScN presents broad prospects for energy‐efficient computing and sensing hardware, accelerating the development of artificial intelligence (AI).

title: Polyzwitterion with Imidazole for Ultralow‐Power Organic Photoelectric Synaptic Transistors Achieving Multicolor Robot Vision and Dynamic Recognition
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Neuromorphic in‐sensor vision demands photoelectric synaptic transistors that co‐localize optical sensing and electrically tunable plasticity in a compact device, thereby simplifying artificial visual sensing circuits. Electrolytes and ionic liquids are widely employed as dielectric layers for neuromorphic transistors; however, cation–anion pairs without covalent bonds typically suffer from ion‐migration, ion replacement, and electrochemical reactions. These processes lead to current leakage, elevated power consumption, and irreversible drift, while photo‐modulation is further attenuated by exciton–polaron quenching. Here, to stabilize ionic charges and suppress ion‐migration, a polyzwitterion, poly(3‐(1‐vinyl‐3‐imidazolyl)‐propanesulfonate), is used as a single medium to unify electro‐ and photo‐synaptic functions, thereby simplifying the components and interfaces of the multilayer device. The aromatic conjugated imidazole ring stabilizes the cationic charge, and the covalently tethered cation–anion pair prevents long‐distance ion‐migration, ensuring strong cation–anion dipole polarization and reversible charge trapping. This enables robust multi‐wavelength photo‐synaptic modulation coupled with electro‐synaptic plasticity. The resulting organic photoelectric synaptic transistors achieve ultralow event energy consumption down to 10.95 aJ and support application‐relevant in‐sensor demonstrations, including encrypted image decoding, color‐guided robotic manipulation, pedestrian‐speed recognition, and motion prediction. These findings are poised to accelerate the development of multifunctional photoelectric synaptic devices and integrated sensing‐computing hardware architectures for artificial visual systems.

title: Engineered Excited‐State Coupling Enables Efficient Exciton Harvesting in Binuclear Copper Iodide Cluster Scintillators
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Environmentally benign scintillators with broadband radioluminescence are highly desirable for low‐cost, high‐performance x‐ray imaging. Recently, copper iodide (Cu–I) clusters have emerged as promising candidates, owing to strong spin‐orbit coupling, favorable solution processability, excellent x‐ray absorption efficiency, and efficient exciton harvesting enabled by aggregation‐induced emission and thermally activated delayed fluorescence. However, the mechanism by which aggregation‐state variation enhances the light yield by modulating intermolecular interactions remains poorly understood. Here, we establish a pair of isomeric Cu–I clusters with nearly identical x‐ray attenuation coefficients as a model platform to isolate and elucidate the role of intermolecular coupling. In this context, we uncover a breakthrough mechanistic picture in which engineered excited‐state coupling accelerates carrier relaxation and promotes efficient exciton harvesting and radiative recombination. Guided by this mechanism, water‐resistant cluster scintillator glasses with excellent processing flexibility are fabricated, delivering a high light yield of 32,456 photons MeV
                    −1
                    and spatial resolution of 33.6 lp mm
                    −1
                    . Furthermore, tandem integration with a high‐Z scintillator enables selective density‐discriminating x‐ray imaging and micro‐computed tomography. This work provides mechanistic guidance for ligand engineering in the design of efficient cluster scintillators and facilitates the high‐throughput development of promising metal‐cluster complexes for advanced optoelectronic applications.

title: Sequential Crystallization Decouples Cs4PbBr6 and CsPbBr3 Phases Enabling Efficient Perovskite Light‐Emitting Diodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Cesium lead bromide has emerged as a leading candidate for high‐performance perovskite light‐emitting diodes (PeLEDs) in next‐generation optoelectronics. However, the formation of the 0D Cs
                    4
                    PbBr
                    6
                    phase often accompanies CsPbBr
                    3
                    crystallization and is difficult to regulate, hampering the efficiency of LED devices in scalable production. In particular, 0D and 3D perovskite phases often crystallize as disordered structures, leading to poor crystalline quality and a high density of defects in the perovskite films. To address this challenge, we employed an additive‐mediated sequential crystallization (AMSC) strategy using 3‐carboxyphenylphosphonic acid (3‐CPPA) to modulate the crystallization kinetics of the 0D and 3D phases. Through strong interactions between the additive and perovskite precursors, the initial CsPbBr
                    3
                    formation is effectively slowed, allowing for temporally separated crystallization of Cs
                    4
                    PbBr
                    6
                    and CsPbBr
                    3
                    phases. This separated crystallization process significantly enhances the film quality of CsPbBr
                    3
                    phase. Remarkably, the AMSC strategy drives the Cs
                    4
                    PbBr
                    6
                    phase toward the film surface, thereby forming a favorable surface morphology and effectively improving the light outcoupling efficiency of PeLEDs. By leveraging this synergic strategy, we achieve an ultrahigh photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) reaching nearly 100% and realize an efficient external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 35.3% in green PeLEDs, underscoring the critical role of phase crystallization engineering in optimizing perovskite emitters.

title: Electronic Coupling and Dual‐Spillover Effect in Co/Co7Fe3 Heterointerface for Boosting Nitrate‐to‐Ammonia Conversion
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Rational design of dual‐site catalysts to decouple complex multi‐electron pathways is crucial for efficient electrocatalytic nitrate (NO
                    3

                    3
                    RR). Here, we construct a Co/Co
                    7

                    3
                    −

Experimental and theoretical investigations demonstrate that the interfacial electric field modulates the local water network, accelerating water dissociation and ensuring a robust proton supply via hydrogen spillover. Benefiting from well‐defined heterointerfaces, the adsorption energetics of key intermediates are favorably optimized, endowing Co/Co
