title: Axial Cl‐Coordinated Porous FeCoZn Trimetallic Single‐Atom Catalysts: Breaking the Linear Scaling Relation for Superior Oxygen Reduction Reaction and Ultrastable Zinc‐Air Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Single‐atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as a research frontier in electrocatalysis. However, conventional SACs possess single metal active sites, which hardly break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of M–N
                    4
                    . To address this limitation, porous trimetallic single‐atom catalysts (TACs) is fabricated via ZIF‐8‐derived ion exchange and gas‐phase etching methods. The catalyst features Fe, Co, and Zn single atoms with a special M–N
                    4
                    configuration where the three metal atoms share one N ligand. And axial coordination structure exists between Zn and Cl atoms. It exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction activity and stability under acidic/alkaline conditions, with a half‐wave potential of 0.81 V/0.96 V and loss of 4 mV/8 mV after 30 000 cycles. Only 6.5% performance decay is observed after 2163 h of charge‐discharge cycling in zinc‐air batteries (ZABs). Physicochemical characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that the trimetallic configuration breaks the geometric and electronic structural symmetry, optimizing the adsorption of intermediates during the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Axial coordination of Cl on Zn facilitates the bridge‐type adsorption of O
                    2
                    and breaks the linear scaling relationship. This work offers a novel strategy to break the symmetry of geometric and electronic structure of SACs and regulate reaction pathways.

title: Targeting Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress‐ROS‐Inflammation Cycle With Antibacterial Heterojunctions for Periodontitis Therapy
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    In periodontitis, recalcitrant biofilms and the vicious endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle cause persistent inflammatory osteolysis. However, current treatments mainly alleviate infection and inflammation, without targeting this ER stress‐centered etiological circuit. Herein, we report the de novo design of an ER‐regulating heterojunction (ERR‐HJ), composed of cobalt selenide (CoSe), Ti
                    3
                    C
                    2
                    MXene, and taurine, for periodontitis treatment via bacterial clearance, ER homeostasis maintenance, and alveolar bone regeneration. Our studies demonstrate that the unique structure of the CoSe/Ti
                    3
                    C
                    2
                    heterojunction can scavenge ROS and easily transfer electrons from H
                    2
                    O
                    2
                    to bacterial membranes, which disrupts bacterial respiration and metabolism. At the cellular level, the heterojunction with taurine activates selenoprotein metabolism, restores redox balance, and alleviates ER stress by dampening the PERK‐CHOP pathway, collectively reprogramming macrophages towards a tissue‐regenerative M2 phenotype while inhibiting their osteoclastogenic differentiation. Strikingly, the osteogenic differentiation of human periodontal ligament cells is profoundly boosted. In periodontitis models, the ERR‐HJ promotes tissue repair and reduces alveolar bone resorption through concomitant suppression of oxidative stress, ER stress, and inflammation, suggesting the disruption of the self‐perpetuating cycle. This work furnishes an intriguing avenue for developing innovative heterojunction biomaterials to treat bacterial infection‐associated disorders by integrating bacterial killing and ER stress‐ROS‐inflammation cycle inhibition.

title: Direct observations of submesoscale turbulence driving mesoscale eddy leakage
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Understanding oceanic transport and material fate has long relied on observations that primarily resolve mesoscale, largely geostrophic flows, leaving the role of submesoscale turbulence comparatively unobserved and poorly understood. Here, using new high-resolution drifter-cluster experiments with closest initial spacings below 1 km, we provide direct Lagrangian observations of how submesoscale turbulence modifies mesoscale eddy coherence and transport pathways. The clustered drifters resolve intense, transient ageostrophic motions that are fundamentally absent from geostrophic descriptions of eddy behavior. Analyzed in an eddy-centered reference frame, the observations reveal pronounced submesoscale-driven radial dispersion that facilitates substantial water-mass exchange between the eddy core and its periphery in both the mixed layer and the subsurface. Quantitative estimates indicate submesoscale horizontal diffusivity of
                    O
                    (10 to 100) m
                    2
                    /s and a nonlocal dispersion regime across submesoscales. These results challenge the traditional view of mesoscale eddies as coherent structures containing a persistent water mass, with broad implications for interpreting and predicting the transport and fate of tracers in the ocean.

title: Loss of KAT5-dependent H2A.Z acetylation provokes chromosomal instability in recurrent pregnancy loss
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Placenta defects are one of the major causes of miscarriages, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. We demonstrate that trophoblast-specific depletion of the acetyltransferase
                    Kat5
                    , or introduction of acetylation-defective mutants
                    Kat5-Q377E G380E
                    and
                    Kat5-Y47A
                    , induces severe chromosomal instability (CIN) during trophoblast cells division, leading to embryonic lethality. Moreover, mutation of a key lysine acetyltransferase 5 (KAT5) substrate, H2A.Z, via the introduction of
                    H2az1-K5R K8R K12R K14R
                    (which prevents H2A.Z acetylation), phenocopies the effects of KAT5 loss. Integrated RNA sequencing and CUT&Tag in mouse trophoblast stem cells reveal that KAT5, through H2A.Z acetylation, regulates transcription of key mitotic genes (
                    Aurka
                    ,
                    Aurkb
                    , and
                    Cenpa
                    ). We extend our finding to human trophoblast stem cells, demonstrating a conserved role for KAT5 in preventing CIN. Clinical analysis of placental villi from recurrent pregnancy loss patients with copy number variations revealed reduced expression of KAT5 and acetylated H2A.Z. This study demonstrates that the conserved KAT5–H2A.Z acetylation pathway safeguards chromosomal stability in trophoblast cells, supporting placenta development and successful pregnancy.

title: High-throughput droplet-based enzymatic DNA methylome profiling enables single-cell resolution of epigenetic heterogeneity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: DNA methylation is a fundamental epigenetic modification that regulates gene expression, cellular identity, and disease-associated regulatory programs. However, high-throughput single-cell DNA methylation technologies have been limited by DNA degradation, low CpG recovery, and the poor scalability of bisulfite-based methods. Here, we present scEM-seq, a droplet-based single-cell enzymatic methylome sequencing method that integrates barcode ligation within a single emulsification step, followed by postemulsion cytosine-to-uracil conversion. This design substantially reduces DNA loss and enables robust profiling of tens of thousands of single cells per experiment. scEM-seq generates high-quality single-cell methylomes with moderately improved CpG coverage and balanced read utilization compared with other droplet-based microfluidic methods. Applied to peripheral blood mononuclear cells, scEM-seq accurately resolves major immune lineages, and in prostate cancer tissues, it reveals diverse malignant cell states and patient-specific epigenetic and copy number architectures. scEM-seq enables scalable single-cell dissection of epigenetic heterogeneity across diverse biological and disease contexts, broadening the scope of DNA methylation–based studies into cellular regulation and disease.

title: Histone methyltransferase NSD2 shapes CD8+ T cell fates through the H3K36me2-Zbtb20 axis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
CD8
                    +
                    T cells, as the most important cytolytic cells in adaptive immunity, can differentiate into distinct subpopulations with specific functions and fates. During this process, CD8
                    +
                    T cells exhibit substantial plasticity in their differentiation trajectory. Notably, epigenetic regulation has emerged as a pivotal mechanism to govern T cell fate decisions. In this study, we demonstrate that the histone methyltransferase NSD2 critically regulates CD8
                    +
                    T cell differentiation during acute viral infection. While NSD2 deficiency enhances the early expansion of activated CD8
                    +
                    T cells, it severely compromises their survival fitness during the contraction phase, leading to a disproportionate collapse of the antigen-specific pool and limiting the establishment of robust long-lived memory. Mechanistically, this defect is driven by the disruption of the H3K36me2-
                    Zbtb20
                    regulatory axis. Furthermore, we show that in the absence of NSD2, CD8
                    +
                    T cells in tumor exhibit an increased proportion but dysfunctional resident memory T cell phenotype. Collectively, our findings highlight a critical role for NSD2 in providing more mechanistic insights into how epigenetic mechanisms fine-tune T cell differentiation.

title: RAF isoform selectivity of MEK inhibitors and rational design of a covalent ARAF-MEK inhibitor
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Aberrant activation of the RAS/RAF/mitogen-activated protein kinase kinase (MEK)/extracellular signal–regulated kinase pathway is a frequent cause of cancer. Allosteric MEK inhibitors block this pathway by binding RAF-MEK complexes to prevent activation of MEK by RAF. However, how MEK inhibitor potency varies across the three RAF isoforms remains poorly understood. We profiled seven allosteric MEK inhibitors and observed a notable hierarchy of sensitivity: All most potently inhibited CRAF-driven MEK activation while relatively sparing ARAF-driven activation. We identified point mutations in ARAF and CRAF proximate to the MEK inhibitor binding site that markedly altered inhibitor sensitivity. Using a rational design approach, we developed a more potent inhibitor of ARAF-driven MEK signaling, TWG-07-148. Our cryo–electron microscopy structure shows how this acrylamide-containing analog of MEK inhibitor trametinib covalently targets Cys
                    514
                    , a residue unique to ARAF. Our studies highlight the importance of the activating RAF isoform as a determinant of MEK inhibitor sensitivity and provide proof of concept for the development of MEK inhibitors that more effectively block ARAF-driven MEK signaling via covalent targeting of Cys
                    514
                    .

title: Scalable architecture for measurement-induced squeezed light interferometers
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Scalable interferometers lie at the heart of photonic quantum technologies, but their expansion has been fundamentally limited by optical losses that grow with circuit depth. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a measurement-induced architecture for multimode squeezed-light interferometers that overcomes this barrier. By shifting complexity from deep optical networks to programmable homodyne measurements, we realize effective transformations within a shallow, low-loss platform. We validate the principle with a six-mode device and extend it to a 400-mode interferometer, marking a leap in scale beyond conventional designs. Crucially, this strategy not only enables scalable squeezed light interferometry but also provides a powerful route to the generation of large-scale entangled states—a key requirement for quantum computing, simulation, and communication. Our results establish measurement-induced circuits as a practical pathway toward noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) applications and future demonstrations of quantum advantage.

title: SCML2 inhibits PrimPol-mediated DNA replication repriming and regulates replication gap-associated cancer cell vulnerability
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
PrimPol-mediated fork repriming generates single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) gaps during DNA damage tolerance (DDT), which, if not properly repaired, can threaten genomic stability. PrimPol is a highly error-prone polymerase. Thus, PrimPol activity should be tightly regulated to fit into DDT and remain low during unstressed DNA replication. Human sex comb on midleg like-2 (SCML2), a Polycomb protein containing MBT repeats, has been identified as a component of the noncanonical PRC1 complex and a regulator of p53 and CHK1 stability. Here, we show that SCML2A is a suppressor of PrimPol. SCML2A directly binds two domains of PrimPol: Its RBR domain binds the C terminus of PrimPol, and its SAM domain binds the amino-terminal AEP domain, thereby inhibiting ssDNA-binding capacity of the AEP domain. SCML2 depletion leads to increased nascent DNA synthesis and accumulation of PrimPol-mediated ssDNA gaps under replication stress. SCML2 depletion also enhances PrimPol engagement during unstressed DNA replication, leading to subsequent accumulation of ssDNA gaps, which are filled by REV1/POLζ-mediated translesion synthesis (TLS) and RAD51-mediated template switching (TS). SCML2 depletion confers cellular hypersensitivity to RAD51 or REV1/POLζ inhibition, which is associated with increased accumulation of ssDNA gaps. Furthermore, CDK2 phosphorylates SCML2A at Ser
                    267
                    , which suppresses RBR-mediated PrimPol interaction. Cyclin E1 overexpression leads to CDK2-mediated SCML2A Ser
                    267
                    hyperphosphorylation, which releases the inhibitory effect of SCML2A on PrimPol and subsequently induces ssDNA gap accumulation. Collectively, we identify SCML2A as a negative regulator of PrimPol.

title: Action features dominate cortical representation during natural vision
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Cortical resources are allocated into systems specialized for processing ecologically relevant features of the world. These features are typically studied in isolation using controlled experimental stimuli, making it difficult to assess the relative importance of different kinds of features that tend to overlap during natural vision. In the current study, we evaluated the relative contributions of action, agent, and scene features in predicting cortical activity while participants viewed a 1-h nature documentary. We tested four sets of model features: semantic vectors capturing the observed action, agent, and scene features derived from an annotation of the stimulus, as well as low-level visual motion-energy features. We used banded ridge regression to fit vertex-wise encoding models from the combination of all four sets of features. While each set of features predicted neural activity in the expected areas, the action features predicted more widespread activity. A variance partitioning analysis revealed that the action features captured the most unique variance in neural activity across a much larger extent of cortex than the agent or scene features. Our findings suggest that cortical activity during dynamic, natural vision is dominated by features for understanding the actions of others.

title: Lineage-specific and gestational age–dependent DNA methylation programming orchestrates human placental development
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The human placenta is essential for pregnancy, yet the dynamic regulation of its DNA methylome during development remains poorly understood. To address this, we generated a single base–resolution DNA methylation atlas of human placental trophoblasts across gestation. We identified a lineage-specific methylation program established immediately after implantation, followed by gestational age–dependent methylation accumulation. This program acted as a developmental barrier that coordinated placental maturation and immune homeostasis. By integrating histone modifications and functional perturbations, we revealed a temporal dynamic between H3K27me3 and DNA methylation that silenced proinflammatory loci and a switch from H3K9me3 to DNA methylation at repeat elements to maintain genome stability. Aberrant methylation in preterm placentas underscored the physiological importance of methylation regulation. Using human trophoblast stem cells, we demonstrated that
                    DNMT1
                    was critically required for maintaining trophoblast methylome integrity and self-renewal, while the DNMT3 family were equally essential for trophoblast survival. Overall, we established a placenta-specific epigenetic framework for human trophoblast development.

title: An in situ forming immunomodulatory hydrogel reinvigorates exhausted CD8+ T cells via preserving their mitochondrial fitness
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
CD8
                    +
                    T cell exhaustion driven by mitochondrial dysfunction remains a major barrier to effective cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report an in situ forming
                    d
                    -α-tocopheryl polyethylene glycol succinate (TPGS)–based hydrogel [multifunctional thermosensitive composite gel (MTC Gel)] that reinvigorates exhausted CD8
                    +
                    T cells by preserving mitochondrial fitness through a two-pronged strategy. After intratumoral injection, MTC Gel rapidly undergoes gelation at physiological temperature and dissociates to generate a high local concentration of TPGS, which targets cancer cell mitochondria to trigger prodeath mitophagy. This process induces robust immunogenic cell death (ICD) and blocks tunneling nanotube–mediated mitochondrial hijacking. Meanwhile, NLG919-loaded hybrid nanoparticles released from MTC Gel synergistically restore mitochondrial biogenesis in CD8
                    +
                    T cells suppressed by indoleamine 2,3-dioxygenase 1. Across multiple murine tumor models, MTC Gel reprograms T cell immunity by reducing CD8
                    +
                    T cells exhaustion while enhancing effector and cytotoxic functions, thereby eliciting potent tumoricidal activity. These findings highlight this rationally designed hydrogel system as a clinically translatable platform for next-generation ICD-based cancer immunotherapies.

title: A functional two-pore-domain K+ channel from a large DNA virus
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The evolutionary history of proteins helps to understand their structure/function correlates and suggests on how functional complexity evolved from primitive precursors. In the superfamily of K
                    +
                    channels, functional features of complex eukaryotic inward rectifier (Kir) channels and voltage-dependent (Kv) channels could be understood in terms of an increase in structural complexity of their prokaryotic precursors. K2P channels, which are made from tandem repeats of two pore domains, are not found in prokaryotes and their evolutionary origin is still unknown. In searching for primitive K2P channel precursors, we screened the genomes of nucleocytoplasmic large DNA viruses (NCLDVs) for genes coding for K2P channels. This was motivated by two reasons: NCLDVs are already known for coding primitive Kir type channels, and they play important roles in the evolution of eukaryotes. Here, we report that the NCLDV
                    Pyramimonas orientalis
                    virus codes for K2P-like K
                    +
                    channels. With only 178 amino acids and no cytosolic domains, this Kpov protein is much smaller than any eukaryotic K2P channel, but still functional as K
                    +
                    selective channel in lipid bilayers. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Kpov is not the product of molecular piracy from the host but may result from fusion of primitive viral K
                    +
                    channel pore domains.

title: Morphological intelligence for dynamic aerial interactions
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Biological flyers achieve ecological dominance not through flight alone, but by seamlessly integrating aerial locomotion with forceful physical interactions, including snatching prey, perching on irregular surfaces, and operating across diverse media. Translating this agility into aerial robotics demands reconciling a fundamental conflict: impulsive, high-force actions destabilize the flight platform. Here, we present a bio-inspired unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) equipped with a mechanically intelligent impulsive limb that resolves this tradeoff through physical decoupling. An asymmetric bistable impulse module delivers a 2.3-fold extension within 70 ms, while a soft-linkage architecture reduces the transmission of impulsive interaction forces to the airframe. For the tested seven-segment configuration, intrinsic geometric tolerance corresponds to a passive vertical accommodation range of approximately 70% of the fully deployed arm length, reducing the need for precise altitude regulation within the tested range. We demonstrate the system’s multimodal capacity through dynamic in-flight snatching, energy-efficient perching, high-impact solid fracture, and cross-medium capture in viscous fluids, establishing a new paradigm for UAVs executing physically demanding tasks in complex environments.

title: CASTOR1 functional inactivation drives KRAS-mutant NSCLC and therapy resistance by a noncanonical mechanism of tumor suppression
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
CASTOR1, a cytosolic arginine sensor and regulator of mTORC1 signaling, is identified here as a tumor suppressor in
                    KRAS
                    -driven non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In a
                    
                      KRAS
                      G12D
                    
                    mouse model,
                    CASTOR1
                    deletion enhances tumor initiation and progression, accompanied by increased proliferation. Although CASTOR1 is rarely mutated or deleted in human cancers, its expression progressively declines during tumor progression and is associated with increased AKT activation and CASTOR1 phosphorylation, consistent with functional inactivation. Loss of CASTOR1 results in constitutive mTORC1 hyperactivation, impaired arginine-dependent regulation of mTORC1 signaling, elevated p-4EBP1 and p-S6 levels, increased AKT and ERK activation, genomic instability, and resistance to KRAS
                    G12D
                    inhibitors. Tumors and tumor-derived organoids deficient in CASTOR1 are resistant to KRAS inhibition, but this resistance can be overcome by cotargeting mTORC1 or dual PI3K/mTOR inhibition. These findings identify CASTOR1 as a critical link between nutrient sensing and oncogenic signaling and reveal its functional inactivation as an important mechanism contributing to
                    KRAS
                    -driven NSCLC progression and therapeutic resistance. The results further support rational combination therapies to overcome KRAS inhibitor resistance in CASTOR1-low NSCLC.

title: Primary tumor–derived lactate primes prostate cancer cells for a dormant fate
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The metastatic outcome depends on the state of disseminated cancer cells (DCCs) leading to overt metastasis or undergoing dormancy. Before distant organ colonization, primary tumor microenvironment may shape the decision between proliferation and dormancy. Here, we identify lactic acid (LA), a highly abundant environmental metabolite at the primary site in prostate cancer (PCa), as a key inducer of dormant state. LA-uploading PCa cells undergo a proliferation delay, associated with stemness, therapy tolerance, and invasiveness through the nuclear receptor subfamily 2 group F member 1 (COUP-TF1/NR2F1) activation. These traits rely on LA-driven accumulation of lipid droplets (LDs), which serve as reservoirs of lipid-derived acetyl moieties essential for histone acetylation. Notably, the epigenetic reader BRD4 is essential for COUP-TF1 expression and for establishing and maintaining dormancy. In metastatic sites, where LA levels are low, dormant features are lost, allowing DCCs to support metastatic growth. Last, targeting LA-mediated LD formation or BRD4 activation prevents dormancy entry, reducing PCa cell adaptability and increasing vulnerability to antiproliferative therapies.

title: NRF2 coordinates cystine import and glutathione use to sustain ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance in cancer
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Cancer cells must balance detoxification of reactive metabolic by-products while preserving redox homeostasis, but how this trade-off is managed remains unclear. The Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (KEAP1)–nuclear factor–erythroid 2–related factor 2 (NRF2) pathway, a key regulator of antioxidant defenses, is frequently hyperactivated in cancer. Formaldehyde, a genotoxic one-carbon by-product, is typically detoxified via glutathione (GSH), which is also essential for suppressing ferroptotic cell death. Here, we show that NRF2 promotes formaldehyde tolerance through up-regulation of the cystine transporter SLC7A11, enabling a protective mechanism that is largely independent of GSH, which remains necessary for ferroptosis resistance. In NRF2-active cells, formaldehyde reacts with cysteine to form a thiazolidine conjugate, and the combination of formaldehyde stress and SLC7A11 inhibition activates the integrated stress response, suppresses global protein synthesis, and markedly compromises cell viability. Together, these findings reveal that NRF2 coordinates ferroptosis resistance and formaldehyde tolerance, exposing a cancer vulnerability through combined inhibition of cystine uptake and GSH synthesis.

title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the
                    Escherichia coli
                    –containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest
                    E. coli
                    signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

title: Susumu Tonegawa (1939–2026): A molecular biologist who transformed immunology and neuroscience
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Susumu Tonegawa transformed two fields of biology. His discovery of the genetic mechanism generating antibody diversity established the foundations of modern immunology and earned him the 1987 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Remarkably, he then began a second scientific career in neuroscience, pioneering genetic approaches to dissect the molecular and circuit mechanisms of learning and memory and, ultimately, the neuronal ensembles that store specific memories. He was also an ambitious institution builder whose leadership shaped neuroscience at Massachusetts Institute of Technology and RIKEN. As former trainees from his immunology and neuroscience labs, we remember a scientist of extraordinary curiosity, intensity, and intellectual courage, who was never afraid to leave familiar territory in pursuit of a fundamental question.

title: Polycomb factor PHF19 affects AML initiation, patient prognosis, and survival
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is marked by unchecked expansion of undifferentiated myeloid cells. Although oncogenic fusions such as MLL-AF9 can initiate disease, the early steps of leukemogenesis and the role of cell-intrinsic regulators remain unclear. We previously showed that the Polycomb-associated factor Phf19 is required for hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) maintenance and state control in mice and that its loss (Phf19
                    KO
                    ) impairs HSC function. To define Phf19’s role in transformation, we expressed MLL-AF9 in Phf19
                    KO
                    hematopoietic cells and performed integrated multiomic analyses. Phf19 deletion promoted acquisition of stemlike features and reduced responsiveness to differentiation-inducing AML therapies. Molecular and functional consequences of Phf19 loss paralleled those observed in the datasets of patients with AML. From these data, we derived a prognostic signature—PHFScore—which reveals previously unrecognized AML survival-correlating genes that robustly stratify patients across distinct cellular origins and leukemogenic stages, underscoring Phf19’s key role in AML biology and prognosis.

title: Structural basis for start codon selection by eIF5-mimic proteins
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Start codon selection extensively regulates the cellular proteome and is implicated in cancer and other diseases. The eIF5-mimic proteins (5MPs: 5MP1/BZW2 and 5MP2/BZW2) restrict non-AUG start codon usage and thereby reprogram proteoform expression from mRNAs with alternative start sites, such as the oncogenic c-Myc. Here, using in extracto cryo–electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and biochemical assays, we report how 5MP represses translation dependent on the sequence context at start codons. Cryo-EM structures of 48
                    S
                    preinitiation complexes (PICs) reveal 5MP1 bound at the A site of the small ribosomal subunit. 5MPs act as initiation factors that stabilize an open PIC conformation, promoting mRNA scanning and inhibiting initiation at suboptimal start codons. We propose to designate 5MP as eIF1S (eukaryotic initiation factor 1 scanning). These findings reveal the structural basis for proteome modulation by 5MPs and may help correct dysregulated translation in disease.

title: Learning by moving: Physical motion accelerates category learning
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Categorization is crucial for survival, helping animals forage, navigate, and avoid predators—all tasks involving movement. Yet, dominant theories of category learning treat it as a purely cognitive or perceptual process. Here, we challenge this view by demonstrating that physical movement can enhance category learning—but selectively. Using immersive virtual reality, we found that performing large actions, such as swinging a lightsaber, substantially improved learning of categories requiring integration of multiple cues (e.g., distinguishing aggressive from noncancerous lesions), while having minimal impact on categories involving independent evaluation of features (e.g., sorting by color and shape). This selective enhancement reveals a previously unrecognized motor contribution to categorization and may explain why prior studies missed it, opening avenues for optimizing training in critical categorization tasks.

title: An innovative colon inflammation-targeting platform for ulcerative colitis treatment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The therapeutic options for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have recently expanded substantially. Tofacitinib, an oral small-molecule inhibitor of Janus kinase (JAK), recently FDA approved for ulcerative colitis, represented a paradigm shift in a field previously dominated by biologics. Tofacitinib, however, carries a black box warning for major adverse cardiovascular events, an elevated risk of malignancies, risk of blood clots, and pulmonary embolism. In addition, tofacitinib is avoided in pregnancy and used with caution in women of child bearing age due to potential risks to the developing fetus. Notably, these potential complications are all due to the systemic distribution of tofacitinib. To address these issues, we developed Lipo-tm-HA, a liposomal platform incorporating mannitol (m) and hyaluronic acid (HA) for targeting tofacitinib (t) to the inflamed colon. We characterized Lipo-tm-HA and have shown that it (i) remains stable in gastric conditions due to HA coating, (ii) adheres to transferrin in inflamed mucosa due to its negative charge, and (iii) enhances macrophage uptake through mannose receptor–mediated endocytosis. Due to targeting, we show that a single oral administration of Lipo-tm-HA at a dose of 10 milligrams per kilogram is superior in efficacy compared with daily treatment with free tofacitinib in a dextran sodium sulfate–induced colitis model. Collectively, our innovative formulation will enable colonic inflammation targeting, reduce systemic exposure, and allow administration of decreased doses.

title: Biophysically constrained learning from healthy neural priors improves motor decoding in pathological cortical networks
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
High-performance brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) rely on stable neural representations, yet brain functional impairments inherently disrupt canonical encoding, creating a fundamental decoding paradox. Conventional data-driven approaches struggle to bridge this gap because of pathological data scarcity and heterogeneity. Here, we propose to leverage healthy neural priors and introduce Pathology-Aware Consensus Training (PACT), a paradigm embedding biophysical constraints into healthy neural recordings to guide neural decoding. In a gesture classification task using high-density electrocorticography from patients with gliomas infiltrating the motor cortex, PACT improved the accuracy by more than 10%, effectively restoring the distorted semantic geometry of motor commands and realigning them with healthy canonical representations (correlation increase:
                    r
                     = 0.66 to
                    r
                     = 0.94). Mechanistically, PACT induced an emergent “inverse weighting” strategy: The model autonomously suppresses high-power pathological noise while reanchoring spatial attention to functional compensatory regions. This study provides a proof of concept for improving decoding in compromised networks by harnessing healthy neural dynamics, laying the theoretical foundation for future BCI deployments in clinical populations.

title: A noncanonical meiotic cohesin complex associates with specific MCM complexes to promote cohesion establishment and homolog bias
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
A meiosis-specific cohesin complex is essential for the segregation of homologous chromosomes and sister chromatids during meiosis, yet its composition and mechanism in
                    Drosophila
                    remain elusive. Here, we demonstrate that SOLO directly interacts with SUNN, SSEP, and SMC1 and that these interactions are conserved between
                    Drosophila melanogaster
                    and
                    Zeugodacus cucurbitae
                    , a Tephritidae species within Diptera. SOLO associates with SMC1 via specific conserved residues within its highly conserved carboxyl-terminal domain. Furthermore, SOLO directly interacts with the MCM4 and MCM6 subunits of the MCM complex and with MMS22L to establish cohesion; consequently, postreplicative expression of SOLO results in a complete function loss. SOLO also interacts with the MEI-217 and MEI-218 subunits of the meiosis-specific minichromosome maintenance complex to promote homolog bias during meiosis. We propose that in Diptera, an evolutionarily diverged meiotic cohesin complex, composed of SOLO, SUNN, SSEP, SMC1, and SMC3, interacts with various complexes to fulfill its diverse meiotic functions.

title: Spider-inspired bidirectional robotic joints driven by electrohydraulic multiaxial strain
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Compared with conventional motors and servos, soft-actuated angular-motion devices are superior in environmental adaptability and human-robot interaction, yet they can only achieve active bidirectional angular motion by integrating antagonistic actuators or restriction modules. The integration of such components introduces deformation antagonism, compromises structural simplicity, and increases control complexity. Herein, we propose a spider-inspired centimeter-scale soft bidirectional robotic joint driven by a pair of synchronously controlled electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs). Specifically, the EHAs generate multiaxial strain, enabling the joint to bidirectionally rotate depending on its physical state, without introducing additional functional components or asynchronous controllers. Furthermore, the joint demonstrates (i) high-speed (forward: 2851° per second, reverse: 1934° per second) and wide-stroke (up to 156.8°) rotational performance, (ii) multimodal motion (e.g., self-unfolding, self-folding, and reciprocating swinging), (iii) continuous response (up to 40 hertz), and (iv) payload-bearing capability. Last, three joint-integrated devices validate its feasibility as a multifunctional, high-dynamic, and single-channel-controlled actuation component in diverse robotic applications. This work establishes a viable design framework for minimalist yet versatile bioinspired robots.

title: A methylation-dependent reader couples arginine methylation to S6K2 signaling in vivo
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Arginine methylation regulates diverse cellular processes, yet how methyl-arginine reader proteins couple this modification to kinase signaling in vivo remains poorly defined. Here, we identify staphylococcal nuclease and Tudor domain containing 1 (SND1) as a pancreas-enriched effector that links symmetric dimethylarginine (SDMA) recognition to S6 kinase 2 (S6K2) activation. Disruption of SDMA-mediated binding by a point mutation in the SND1 Tudor domain markedly diminishes ribosomal protein S6 (S6) phosphorylation in the pancreas. Mechanistically, SND1 engages SDMA-modified arginines within the carboxyl-terminal glycine-arginine–rich (GAR) motif of S6K2 and promotes S6K2-dependent S6 phosphorylation. Mice harboring lysine substitutions at these GAR arginines (
                    S6k2
                    RK) phenocopy Snd1 Tudor-mutant (
                    Snd1
                    knock-in) animals, exhibiting impaired pancreatic S6 phosphorylation. Transcriptomic analyses reveal extensive overlap in dysregulated pathways between
                    Snd1
                    and
                    S6k2
                    mutant pancreata, supporting a shared signaling cascade. Together, these findings establish a methylation-dependent reader-kinase axis that links protein arginine methyltransferase 5–catalyzed arginine methylation to tissue-specific control of ribosome signaling and cellular stress adaptation.

title: The Nematostella synaptonemal complex mediates divergent and sex-specific meiotic programs
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Throughout eukaryotes, the synaptonemal complex (SC) is a supramolecular structure essential for meiotic chromosome dynamics and sexual reproduction. While metazoan SC proteins display substantial sequence divergence, the lack of functional analyses beyond bilaterian models has obscured a mechanistic understanding of SC evolution. Here, we report that the sea anemone
                    Nematostella vectensis
                    exhibits synapsis of homologous chromosomes in a classic zipper-like manner and expresses at least eight orthologs of 10 known vertebrate SC proteins. Unexpectedly, mutagenesis of the core SC components
                    sycp1
                    ,
                    syce2
                    , and
                    sycp3
                    resulted in divergent and sexually dimorphic phenotypes, indicating the functional diversification of these conserved factors. Combined, these findings challenge the assumption that the conservation of protein sequence or ultrastructure implies mechanistic homology.

title: SMCHD1 loss rewires MYOD1 enhancer nexuses and chromatin accessibility landscapes in muscle cells
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
SMCHD1 is a chromatin architectural protein linked to heterochromatin repression. Loss of function mutations of SMCHD1 cause facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy type 2 (FSHD2) through activation of the
                    DUX4
                    transcription factor gene. However, it is unknown how SMCHD1 may regulate transcription independently of DUX4. Here, we show that SMCHD1 safeguards enhancer organization within the three-dimensional (3D) genome in human myoblasts. Loss of SMCHD1 leads to widespread gains in chromatin accessibility, aberrant transcription, and selective remodeling of myogenic transcription factor MYOD1 occupancy. Integrative analyses of histone modifications, chromatin accessibility, Hi-C looping, and enhancer-gene modeling reveal that SMCHD1 loss rewires the landscape of clustered enhancers and promotes the emergence of new networks of enhancer elements, termed MYOD1 enhancer nexuses. These structures are marked by increased enhancer connectivity, increased local 3D chromatin interactions, and coordinated activation of genes likely relevant for FSHD pathology. Our findings identify SMCHD1 as a key architectural constraint that suppresses hyperactive enhancer networks, thereby preserving transcriptional homeostasis in myoblasts.

title: 53BP1 as a cofactor in the activation of the p53-family transcriptional program: A correlative multimodal microscopy approach
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Understanding how molecular mechanisms regulate cell function in tissues requires approaches that link phenotypes to mechanisms across different spatial scales. Here, we present automated multimodal multiplexed microscopy for image cytometry (A.M
                    3
                    .I.CO), a correlative imaging platform that combines multiscale resolution, from millimeters to nanometers, with automated workflows for high-throughput phenotypic profiling and targeted single-molecule analysis in situ. Applying A.M
                    3
                    .I.CO, we observed that 53BP1 is recruited at transcribed p53 target genes independently of the activating stimulus, providing evidence for the formation of a putative complex between 53BP1, p53, and the basal transcription machinery in single cells, as also supported by in vivo observations in tumor models. Extending our measurements to p63 and p73, we found that 53BP1 localized at p63- and p73-targeted transcription sites, suggesting a broader role in participating in p53 family–dependent transcription. These findings indicate an additional genome-surveillance pathway in transcriptional control regulating diverse cellular functions while establishing A.M
                    3
                    .I.CO as a platform for spatially resolved functional analysis.

title: In situ CAR-M engineered by liposomal mRNA nanomedicine remodels fibrotic microenvironment for ameliorating liver fibrosis
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Liver fibrosis is a severe complication of diverse chronic liver diseases characterized by a dysregulated hepatic microenvironment, and effective clinical therapeutic strategies for this condition remain lacking to date. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR-Ms) hold considerable therapeutic potential for liver fibrosis via antigen-specific recognition and efferocytotic activity, yet their clinical translation is largely hindered by the sophisticated ex vivo preparation procedures. Herein, we report an in situ CAR-M engineering strategy that uses a phosphatidylserine (PS)–incorporated, macrophage-targeted lipid nanoparticle (LNP) for the codelivery of CAR messenger RNA (mRNA) and Cas9 mRNA in vivo. Our findings demonstrate that this engineered LNP achieves efficient targeting of liver-resident macrophages. Transfection with fibroblast activation protein α (FAPα)–CAR mRNA equips macrophages with the capacity to specifically target activated hepatic stellate cells (aHSCs), whereas Cas9-mediated follistatin-like protein 1 (FSTL-1) gene editing enhances the efferocytotic function of macrophages in liver tissues. Consequently, functional CAR-Ms are generated in situ, which elicits robust antifibrotic effects, including reduced collagen deposition, restored sinusoidal architecture and enhanced immune-mediated antifibrotic activity. Collectively, our customized LNP-mediated in situ engineering of liver macrophages into CAR-Ms enables precise antifibrotic intervention for liver fibrosis and circumvents the cumbersome ex vivo CAR-M preparation process.

title: Early Gravettian genomic data from Western Europe reveal population movements before the LGM
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Anatomically modern humans first settled in Europe at least 45,000 years ago, yet limited genomic data from 45 to 20 thousand years (ka) constrain reconstructions of Upper Palaeolithic population dynamics. Before the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM; ∼26.5 to 19 ka), Gravettian groups (∼34 to 25 ka) were widespread across Europe and genetically diverse, including the Fournol and Věstonice lineages. Here, we present genome-wide data from three Gravettian individuals: two from the Franco-Cantabrian region (Chufín, Spain, and Isturitz, France) and one from Italy (Ostuni1b). Our analyses reveal previously undetected gene flow between eastern and western early Gravettian populations in southwestern Europe, challenging models of regional genetic continuity from the Aurignacian to the Solutrean (∼24 to 19 ka). To investigate population history during the LGM, a period for which human skeletal remains are extremely rare, we analyzed sedimentary ancient DNA from Solutrean Layer 122 at El Mirón Cave (Cantabria, Spain; ∼22,000 calibrated years before the present), recovering ∼14,000 human single-nucleotide polymorphisms. These data support persistence of Fournol-related ancestry in southwestern Europe throughout the LGM.

title: Using initial states to identify successful El Niño–Southern Oscillation forecasts 1 year in advance
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the primary source of climate predictability on seasonal and longer timescales over much of the globe, but predicting its phase beyond 9 months has remained challenging. Here, we leverage an underappreciated factor in ENSO forecasting: the substantial variation in forecast skill based on the ENSO phase at the time a forecast is issued. Our analysis of transitions between ENSO phases in a dynamical hindcast dataset demonstrates that this variation markedly exceeds intermodel differences in predictive capability. Forecasts initialized during La Niña conditions perform best, with three models correctly predicting transitions to El Niño 1 year in advance over 70% of the time. We present our findings in a simple framework that allows decision-makers to assess the likelihood of a forecast being correct on the basis of the current ENSO state. Applied effectively, these findings could improve long-lead ENSO forecasting strategies, enhancing global risk management.

title: Bioinspired ventral-groove fibers for volume-programmable pneumatic actuation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Pneumatic actuation plays a central role in soft robotics, with conventional systems relying on pressure-driven chamber deformation and closed-loop feedback for precise control. Here, we introduce bioinspired ventral-groove filamentary fibers that reframe pneumatic actuation from pressure-dominated chambers to volume-programmable fiber architectures, enabling previously unexplored robotic capabilities. Coupling microgroove unfolding with elastic expansion, these molecularly programmed fibers achieve reversible 400× area expansion at ultralow pressure (∼0.8 kPa) and scale from ∼100 μm to centimeter-scale diameters and tens of meters in length, supporting micro- to macro-scale robotic systems. We demonstrate responsive textile actuation through an everyday flotation garment with 20-m fibers seamlessly integrated into clothing. We also show a gripping approach with three capabilities: disturbance-robust high-precision grasping, conformal handling of fragile nerve-like filaments and delicate incense-ash cones, and open-loop operation that reduces reliance on sensory feedback. By establishing a volume-programmable actuation paradigm, this work paves the way for low-pressure pneumatic technologies in soft robotics and responsive textiles.

title: Frequency-dependent fitness effects are ubiquitous in rapidly adapting microbial populations
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
In simple microbial populations, the fitness effects of selected mutations are typically assumed to be constant, regardless of mutant frequency. This assumption underpins predictions about evolutionary dynamics, epistasis, and the maintenance of genetic diversity. Here, we systematically test this assumption using beneficial mutations from early generations of the
                    Escherichia coli
                    long-term evolution experiment (LTEE). Using flow cytometry–based competition assays, we find that frequency-dependent fitness effects are the norm rather than the exception, occurring in ∼80% of strain pairs tested. Most competitions exhibit negative frequency dependence, where fitness advantages decline as mutant frequency increases. We demonstrate that the strength of frequency dependence is predictable from invasion fitness measurements, which explain approximately half of the biological variation in frequency-dependent slopes. We also observe violations of fitness transitivity in several strain combinations, indicating that competitive outcomes cannot always be predicted from fitness measured against a single reference strain. High-resolution measurements reveal that frequency dependence changes substantially within the growth cycle, with the net per-cycle effect reflecting the balance of opposing dynamics at different growth phases. Our results demonstrate that, even in a model system designed to minimize ecological complexity, subtle interactions between closely related genotypes create frequency-dependent selection that can fundamentally alter evolutionary trajectories.

title: Neural circuitry mediating hypercapnia-induced microarousal and impaired sleep depth
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Sleep disruption in obstructive sleep apnea syndrome is characterized by frequent microarousals and reduced sleep depth, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we show that intermittent hypercapnic air (HA) induces time-locked microarousals, fragments sleep, reduces non–rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep depth, and diminishes rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. HA exposure activates glutamatergic neurons in the nucleus tract solitary (NTS
                    Vglut2
                    ), and their optogenetic or chemogenetic activation is sufficient to trigger arousal and impair sleep. Projection-specific activation reveals that NTS
                    Vglut2
                    projections to the paraventricular nucleus (PVN), parabrachial nucleus (PB), paraventricular thalamus, and locus coeruleus (LC) promote arousal, whereas projections to the PB and LC additionally reduce NREM sleep depth. Inhibition of NTS
                    Vglut2
                    projection to the PVN significantly postpones HA-induced arousal. NTS
                    Vglut2
                    terminals monosynaptically activate corticotropin-releasing hormone neurons in the PVN (PVN
                    CRH
                    ), and inhibition of PVN
                    CRH
                    neurons or knockdown of
                    Slc17a6
                    (encoding Vglut2), but not
                    Crh
                    , delays hypercapnia-induced arousal. These findings identify neural circuits underlying hypercapnia-induced microarousal and reduced sleep depth.

title: Opposing cell-type preferences for binding and replication shape influenza A virus infection in human airways
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Influenza A viruses (IAVs) pose a threat to human health. Although receptor specificity, polymerase adaptation, and airway tropism have been studied extensively, it remains unresolved how they combine to shape tropism in airway epithelia. Here, we show that avian IAVs infect ciliated and secretory cells but preferentially bind to ciliated cells because of higher apical α2,3-linked sialic acid levels. As replication levels are comparable between cell types, this translates into overall preference for ciliated cells. Human IAVs also preferentially bind to ciliated cells despite comparable α2,6-linked sialic acid abundance. Instead, they show higher viral RNA and protein levels in secretory cells, linked to their compatibility with human ANP32 proteins and modestly higher ANP32A/B expression in this cell type, resulting in equal infection levels across cell types. Our findings redefine IAV tropism in the human airway as a stage-resolved process shaped by the interplay between apical glycans, viral binding, polymerase cofactor compatibility, and cell-type–specific replication capacity, moving beyond receptor-centric models.

title: Deconfined criticality between an antiferromagnetic insulator and a nodal d-wave superconductor: A quantum Monte Carlo study
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We present a quantum Monte Carlo study of the transition between the insulating Néel state and the nodal
                    d
                    -wave superconductor on the square lattice at half-filling. We access a regime of frustrated magnetic order without a sign problem using a parton representation of the electron in terms of fermionic spinons and bosonic chargons. Both partons move in a background
                    π
                    -flux (so the electron experiences no net flux) and are coupled to a quantum fluctuating SU(2) lattice gauge field. In contrast to earlier studies directly on the electronic degrees of freedom, we find evidence for a second-order deconfined quantum phase transition at which both the Néel and
                    d
                    -wave superconductivity orders vanish continuously. We compute correlators of the spinon-chargon composite with the same quantum numbers as the electron: we find a gapless Dirac dispersion inside the
                    d
                    -wave superconductor, turning into a gapped dispersion in the antiferromagnet.

title: Interferon-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells protects against congenital Zika virus infection
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Interferon-λ (IFN-λ, type III IFN) mediates antiviral immunity at anatomic barriers, including the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the effects of IFN-λ during congenital Zika virus (ZIKV) infection, we infected mice lacking the IFN-αβ receptor (
                    Ifnar1
                    −/−
                    ) or both the IFN-αβ and IFN-λ receptors (
                    Ifnar1
                    −/−
                    Ifnlr1
                    −/−
                    ) at embryonic day 9 and found that loss of maternal IFN-λ signaling resulted in greater transplacental transmission, highlighting a protective effect of IFN-λ at the maternal-fetal interface. To investigate the spatial relationship between ZIKV infection and antiviral responses, we used HiPlex RNAscope on the entire gravid uterus and found that IFN-λ was expressed more proximal to the site of ZIKV infection in
                    Ifnar1
                    −/−
                    dams compared to
                    Ifnar1
                    −/−
                    Ifnlr1
                    −/−
                    dams. We performed immunophenotyping of the placenta and uterus by flow cytometry and found a decrease in dendritic cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the uterus of
                    Ifnar1
                    −/−
                    Ifnlr1
                    −/−
                    dams compared to
                    Ifnar1
                    −/−
                    dams, but NK cell depletion did not affect fetal infection. Using conditional knockout mice, we identified maternal dendritic cells as the key IFN-λ–responsive cell type mediating protection against ZIKV congenital infection. Together, our data support a model in which IFN-λ signaling to maternal dendritic cells increases dendritic cell accumulation in the uterus, which facilitates a protective antiviral response that restricts ZIKV congenital infection.

title: Hemolymph pressure-mediated friction in the tarsus of the desert locust (Schistocerca gregaria)

title: Gradient-interlayer–based flexible pressure sensors for high-performance robotic perception
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Tactile perception systems based on flexible pressure sensors are indispensable for humanoid robots to perform dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction, and operation in visually challenging environments. Although strategies relying on surface or spatial microstructure engineering have improved sensor performance, the long-standing trade-off among sensitivity, sensing range, and linearity continues to hinder their practical deployment. Inspired by the gradient distribution of mechanoreceptors in human fingertip skin, we report a gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic pressure sensor (GriFIPS) in which a single direct-ink-written elastomeric mesh-like interlayer, with a centrifugal increase in aperture size, is placed between the soft electrode and an ionic hydrogel layer. Operating upstream of the functional layer, the mesh enables progressive, stage-wise contact under increasing load and decouples macroscopic contact-area evolution from the microscopic interfacial response. The sensor simultaneously achieves a sensitivity of 175.9 kPa
                    −1
                    , a linear sensing range up to 360 kPa with a coefficient of determination of 0.997, a low detection limit of about 2.1 Pa, and a response time of about 25 ms, while remaining stable over 6000 loading cycles and 2000 cycles of 50% tensile strain. Building on this single-channel device, we further extend the architecture into a 3-axis gradient-interlayer–based flexible iontronic force sensor (3-axis GriFIFS) capable of resolving triaxial forces and surface textures. When integrated onto a dexterous robotic hand and combined with a temporal convolutional network, the sensors support tactile object recognition, fabric texture discrimination, human–robot interaction, and tactile-guided assembly, offering a generalizable route to tactile sensing for embodied intelligence.

title: Death receptors regulate entry to therapy-induced senescence and orchestrate addiction to IAPs
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Cytotoxic chemotherapy typically results in the elimination of a fraction of the tumor with surviving cells entering a state of persistence or premature replicative senescence that can lead to recurrence. Here, we show that therapy-induced senescence is associated with robust up-regulation of Fas and/or TRAIL-R2/DR5 death receptors in vitro and in vivo. The latter receptors restricted entry to senescence and exerted selective pressure on senescent cells through promoting assembly of proapoptotic receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)/Fas-associated death domain protein (FADD)/Caspase-8 “FADDosome” complexes, restrained by cFLIP
                    L
                    . Accordingly, deletion of
                    CASP-8
                    robustly enhanced entry to senescence and prolonged the life span of senescent cells. cIAP-2, which inhibits death receptor–driven cell death, was also up-regulated in senescent cells, and deletion of IAPs suppressed entry to senescence. Consistent with this, small-molecule IAP antagonists exhibited potent senolytic activity through enhancing death receptor–initiated Caspase-8 activation. Thus, death receptor–driven assembly of RIPK1/FADD/Caspase-8 complexes in senescent cells orchestrates addiction to IAPs that can be exploited by IAP antagonists.

title: TET2-driven activation of AGO2 links epigenetic remodeling to myeloid commitment and leukemia
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
DNA methylation dynamics shape hematopoietic differentiation and leukemogenesis, yet how the dioxygenase TET2—frequently mutated in myeloid malignancies—directs lineage-specific regulatory programs remains unclear. Here, we integrated DNA methylation, chromatin accessibility, three-dimensional (3D) genome architecture, transcriptional profiling, and TET2 chromatin occupancy to define TET2-dependent control of human myeloid commitment. We found that TET2-bound regulatory regions gain short- and long-range chromatin interactions and that a distinct subset of distal, enhancer-enriched sites undergoes TET2-driven demethylation and activation. Among these, we identified and functionally validated an
                    AGO2
                    myeloid-specific intragenic enhancer that is frequently hypermethylated in patients with
                    TET2
                    -mutant acute myeloid leukemia.
                    AGO2
                    expression stratifies patient survival, and AGO2 depletion abrogates leukemic engraftment in vivo. These findings uncover a TET2-AGO2 regulatory axis that integrates epigenetic remodeling, 3D genome reorganization, and leukemic fitness, and they highlight AGO2 as a potential biomarker and therapeutic target in myeloid leukemia.

title: NAD+ metabolic restoration resolves the inflammation-immunocompetence trade-off in lung graft-versus-host disease
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Chronic lung graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) remains difficult to treat, and broad immunosuppression increases infection risk. Single-cell profiling of bronchoalveolar lavage from bronchiolitis obliterans lesions revealed collapse of an epithelial nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD
                    +
                    ) metabolic axis with pathogenic immune-epithelial remodeling, nominating NAD
                    +
                    restoration as an entry point. Because free NAD
                    +
                    is poorly cell-permeable and rapidly consumed, we engineered CaNAD
                    +
                    -PGB-LiP (CNAPL), a high-payload NAD
                    +
                    nanomedicine enabling direct intracellular replenishment. In murine allo-HSCT GVHD, CNAPL improved clinical scores and survival, reduced vascular and epithelial injury, and curtailed hyperinflammation and effector overactivation across GVHD target organs. Unlike immunosuppression, CNAPL preserved phagocytosis, NK/NKT cell (natural killer/natural killer T cell) cytotoxicity, and T cell memory. In posttransplant influenza or
                    Klebsiella
                    infection, CNAPL maintained pathogen control without rekindling GVHD, decoupling inflammation control from infection susceptibility. This metabolism-centered, host-directed strategy restores immune-tissue homeostasis and provides a practical translational path for durable lung GVHD control with preserved antimicrobial defense.

title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA
                    LINC00662
                    through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored
                    LINC00662
                    expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that
                    LINC00662
                    , a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

title: Electrically reconfigurable dipolar polaritons with highly tunable nonlinearity in a homobilayer microcavity
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Active control over optical nonlinearity in solid-state systems is central to unlocking exotic many-body phenomena and photonic devices. While exciton-polaritons in transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) offer a promising platform, their practical utility is impeded by fixed interactions and a trade-off between nonlinearity and oscillator strength. Here, we report electrically tunable dipolar polaritons in a dual-gated bilayer MoS
                    2
                    microcavity, demonstrating in situ reshaping of the dispersion and modulation of the light-matter coupling strength via the quantum-confined Stark effect. Crucially, this electrical control yields a seven-fold enhancement of the polariton-polariton interaction strength. This enhancement arises from the combined tuning of the effective exciton-exciton interaction and the excitonic Hopfield coefficient. In addition, electrostatic doping provides an independent knob to continuously drive a strong-to-weak coupling crossover. Our findings establish dual-gated TMD homobilayer as a versatile platform for on-chip, dynamically reconfigurable nonlinear light-matter physics.

title: Multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor for real-time blood monitoring
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Accurate and real-time monitoring of blood electrolyte composition, particularly sodium (Na
                    +
                    ) and potassium (K
                    +
                    ), is crucial for guiding intraoperative and postoperative decisions, as these ions regulate critical bodily functions such as cardiac rhythm and fluid balance. Current blood analysis relies on ex vivo blood sampling, which introduces substantial time delays and can be susceptible to inaccuracies caused by temperature fluctuations. To address these challenges, we report here a multiplexed and implantable fiber sensor (MIFS) capable of monitoring Na
                    +
                    and K
                    +
                    ions in real time directly in the bloodstream. MIFS integrates three parallel liquid metal channels with a multilayer surface-electrode architecture, which synergistically enhances sensitivity, minimizes sensing drift, ensures mechanical flexibility, and offers outstanding biocompatibility for vascular implantation. In vivo testing in rabbit models and validation in human blood samples demonstrate MIFS’s superior sensing accuracy, real-time, and stable sensing in agreement with conventional ex vivo measurements. This work paves the way for real-time blood monitoring in clinical practice.

title: Si-scRNA-seq: Enabling ambient-stable single-cell transcriptomics through spatially confined biosilicification
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is constrained by rapid RNA degradation during sample storage, necessitating cold-chain logistics. Here we present spatially confined biosilicification (SCB), wherein RNA is encapsulated within a nanoscopic layer of amorphous silicon dioxide, as a highly effective methodology enabling ambient-temperature preservation of single-cell transcriptomes. By judiciously incorporating a silicification inhibitor, SCB achieves spatiotemporal control over both intra- and extracellular silica deposition, preventing excessive crosslinking and cell aggregation while preserving RNA biointegrity and accessibility. scRNA-seq performed with biosilicified cells (Si-scRNA-seq) maintained high transcriptomic fidelity with fresh samples (R
                    2
                    = 0.95 after 7 d) extending RNA half-life to 54.8 d at 25 °C, a 685-fold improvement compared to unprotected samples. Furthermore, Si-scRNA-seq confers robust resistance against oxidative and UV degradation. Compatible with mainstream platforms at ~0.1 RMB per sample, Si-scRNA-seq successfully resolves cellular heterogeneity in clinical lung, liver, and ovarian cancer specimens after extended room-temperature storage. Si-scRNA-seq provides a scalable and cold-chain–free solution for single-cell transcriptomics in research and clinical settings.

title: Contactless continuous guidance of matter in its main states using curved elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Acoustic manipulation uses sound waves to exert force on matter, enabling contactless movement, trapping, and the structuring of particles in bulk media. It offers a contamination-free approach for handling matter in applications spanning across chemistry, biology, and advanced manufacturing. However, state-of-the-art techniques, including acoustic holograms or phased arrays of transducers (PATs) are limited to transporting individual particles or small clusters one by one, and are not suitable for dispersed matter such as gases or aerosols. Here, we introduce a method for guiding a continuous flow of matter along reconfigurable three-dimensional trajectories using elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields (EBAFs). These fields generate converging radial acoustic forces along a programmable path, forming stable mid-air conduits that continuously transport matter. Compared to existing methods such as near-field acoustic levitation, acoustofluidic separation, particle manipulation with vortex and Airy beams, the proposed method offers enhanced versatility, scalability, and real-time control of transport trajectories in mid-air without requiring physical guiding structures. We developed methods to generate EBAFs with PATs tailored to different particle sizes and material properties, and experimentally demonstrated guidance of solids, liquids, aerosols, and gases along programmable trajectories. This technique enables containerless laboratory operations, precise and contamination-free reagent or energy delivery, and integration into advanced additive manufacturing processes that require controlled distribution of matter in different states to target zones.

title: Local growth laws determine global shape of molluscan shells
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Molluscan shells come in various shapes and sizes. Despite this diversity, each species produces a shell with a characteristic shape that is independent of environmental conditions. We seek to understand this robust complexity. We are guided by two principles in the spirit of D’Arcy Thompson. First, the growth is governed by the repeated and continuous application of a fixed growth law, even as the shell evolves in overall shape, without any complex biological machinery to monitor and control the growth. Second, the growth law depends solely on local geometry at the shell’s growing edge. The first principle naturally leads to the mathematical statement that the shape of the shell is generated by the action of a Lie group on a protoconch. The second naturally leads to a particular representation of the Lie group. We use this representation to show that the shapes of nearly all known molluscan shells can be described by essentially three parameters: a scalar (scaling), a vector (orientation), and a curve (edge of the protoconch). We relate these parameters to the phylogenetic tree. In addition to the morphogenetic insight, our results potentially point to a alternative growth-based approach to engineering complex structures.
